_graph: Verdicts for every soft rule: what actually enforces each one today. This file is the answer half of the inventory; verification/controls/soft-rules.json is the extraction half, generated by `graphcheck softrules --write`. A verdict of hard means a machine decides it; record means no decision is possible but a structured record is required; human means the rule is a judgement and stays prose on purpose; open means nothing enforces it and nothing records it.

DEFAULT_MAIN_RSI_IDENTITY.why: 3177 bytes describing when to record friction, when to run the real-model eval, not to poll after activation, and to report the backlog unprompted. No gate reads any of it. Parts are checkable: the receipt already exists, so 'report every such action' is a record that could be required.
DEFAULT_MAIN_RSI_IDENTITY.splits: activation and no-poll are already facts in the receipt; friction discipline and the backlog report are the parts worth making structural.

DEFAULT_COMMON_RULES.why: 19 bullets. Three have gates: comments (the graphcheck comments budget), edit anchoring (the tool schema itself), and repository search (rg ships). The rest - 'write the test before the code', 'choose the test level highest first', 'prefer an existing implementation', 'make every change verifiable', 'take the smallest implementation', 'delete completely' - are methodology with no mechanism.
DEFAULT_COMMON_RULES.enforcedBy: graphcheck comments, the edit tool schema, and the shell itself for three of nineteen bullets.

DEFAULT_WORKER_RULES.why: Most bullets are enforced by the node contract: submit once per execution, structured outputs only, the node file list, restoring files a lane does not own. The two that are not - 'implement the smallest complete change' and 'an edit you have not executed is not evidence' - are judgement.
DEFAULT_WORKER_RULES.enforcedBy: submit validation, output naming, and the workspace commit check.

DEFAULT_MAIN_RULES.why: Two bullets. 'Three blocked rounds then take over' and 'say why you chose the graph shape' are both unenforced; shapeNotes exists in the propose receipt and is advisory.
DEFAULT_MAIN_RULES.splits: the shape reason could become a required, non-empty field on propose_graph; the three-round rule is a judgement about when to stop delegating.

DEFAULT_REVIEWER_RULES.why: The report shape is enforced by core_review_policy.go: verdict, reason and published evidence are required, and files must be non-empty repository-relative paths without '..'. 'Do not inspect the implementation transcript' is half-enforced by the read-only tool surface.

DEFAULT_NODE_PROMPT.why: One valid submit, named outputs, omitted outputs disabled, exact artifact versions, and the commit must identify itself - all enforced by the node runtime.

DEFAULT_MAIN_TOOL_GUIDANCE.why: 'Read a skill before applying it' and 'do not poll after activation' have no check; 'use get_task_status for a compact read' is advisory because both tools exist and either works.
DEFAULT_MAIN_TOOL_GUIDANCE.enforcedBy: the skills gate covers skill format, not whether one was read.

DEFAULT_MAIN_FULL_ACCESS_PROMPT.why: It tells the agent to call propose_system_change and apply_system_change. Both tools were deleted on 2026-11-07; the prompt names tools that no longer exist.
DEFAULT_MAIN_FULL_ACCESS_PROMPT.evidence: No tool named propose_system_change is registered; docs/agent/capabilities.md recorded the removal before it was itself deleted.

DEFAULT_MAIN_APPROVAL_PROMPT.why: Same pair: propose_system_change and apply_system_change, plus 'never edit capability files directly'. The tools are gone, so the instruction cannot be carried out.

DEFAULT_MAIN_FULL_ACCESS_IDENTITY.why: States that full access is active and that gates are open. Every operation already receives this as a generated fact in the briefing; the constant repeats it as prose.
DEFAULT_MAIN_FULL_ACCESS_IDENTITY.enforcedBy: the operation briefing, which reports the actual access policy from the host.

DEFAULT_REVIEWER_TOOL_GUIDANCE.why: 'Never mutate business files' is enforced by the reviewer tool surface, which has no write tool. 'Do not use an implementation transcript' is not enforced at all.

verification/The Complete Guide to pstac.why: An archived third-party article kept as task input with graph:allow-large-file. It states no rule about this repository.
verification/The Complete Guide to pstac.evidence: pstack was removed from the repository and the agent bindings in d3a583dc; this is the last copy.

verification/controls/COVERAGE.generated.why: Produced by verify-graph cover from controls/inventory.json and controls/ledger.json. The data is the source; this table is a rendering.
verification/controls/COVERAGE.generated.evidence: The generator reads inventory.json and ledger.json; deleting the rendering costs nothing as long as cover --write can recreate it.

verification/skills/verify-graph/SKILL.m.why: It teaches a procedure - launch, drive, capture evidence - and the steps are verified by the scenarios and the acceptance tests. It is the on-demand instruction a skill is for, not a rule the repository enforces.
verification/skills/verify-graph/SKILL.m.enforcedBy: skilldoc checks the shape; the journeys check that the steps work.

verification/CONTROL_COVERAGE.md.why: Explains what control coverage means and how to read the ledger. The numbers live in coverage.json.
verification/CONTROL_COVERAGE.md.splits: the definition of a witness belongs in the generated coverage report; the rest is procedure.

verification/skills/verify-graph/CONTROL.why: Schema and worked example for controls/inventory.json. The schema is enforced by the loader, so the document and the code state the same contract.
verification/skills/verify-graph/CONTROL.enforcedBy: the control inventory loader rejects a malformed entry.

examples/README.md.why: Index of the graph examples. FEATURE_MAP.md already lists the routes behind them and the examples themselves are the source.
